transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate you seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I'm here mostly because... well, people keep acting like I'm just imagining things. And I don't want you to think I'm making a fuss or being difficult, I promise I'm not. It's just that I know the hospital people, and some of the folks from the agency where I work—I do housekeeping—I know they've been watching our house. And they keep an eye on my cleaning routes, too. 

I'm pretty sure they just want to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. I try so hard to be a good wife and do everything right for him. I mean, I guess it makes sense they'd want to check on us, right? But it's just been making me a little anxious... is it okay that I feel a little overwhelmed by that?
It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed by all this stress. Along with feeling watched, have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one was around?

Oh... um... I really hope you don't think badly of me for saying this. I know how it must sound, and I promise I'm not... I'm not trying to be dramatic or anything. But... yes. Sometimes, even when the house is completely quiet, I do hear something. Well, a voice. 

It sounds like a woman's voice, usually right near the kitchen window. She tells me to check the locks, or... or to move my husband's pills. It's just so clear, Doctor. Exactly as if she is standing right there next to me. 

I usually just go ahead and check the locks, just to be safe, because I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job taking care of things. That's probably just my mind playing tricks on me because of all the stress you mentioned, right? I hope it's okay that I shared that with you... I just want to be honest so I can be a good patient.
About how long have you been hearing this voice and feeling like you are being watched?

Oh, um... well, I guess it's been a little while. I really hope you don't think I was being irresponsible by not coming in sooner. I just didn't want to be a bother to anyone, and I kept hoping it would just... go away on its own if I worked hard enough. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be a good patient for you—the feeling that people are watching us, and hearing that woman's voice... it's been happening for about 11 months now. Almost a year. I'm so sorry I waited this long to say anything. I hope I'm still doing the right thing by telling you now?
Over this past year, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, feeling down, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try my best to keep a smile on my face, you know? I wouldn't want to bring anyone down or be a burden. 

I still keep busy with my cleaning routes and making sure my husband is comfortable, and I do still really like doing those things. I mean, I get a little anxious sometimes about the people watching, like I mentioned, but... not really sad. I always try to look on the bright side and just keep working hard. 

I hope it's okay that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you been diagnosed with any physical medical conditions or illnesses?

Oh, um... no, I haven't. I'm actually very healthy, physically speaking. I make sure to eat right and stay active with my housekeeping jobs, so... no medical conditions or illnesses at all. 

I really try to take good care of myself so I don't end up in the hospital or anything like that. I wouldn't want to take up a doctor's time if I could help it. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to be doing to stay healthy.
